$comment: The local demo-video toolchain (docs/ai-pipeline/pr-demo-video.md). `factory video install` creates a Python virtualenv under the factory's tools folder, installs these packages at exactly these versions, and downloads the model files by pinned URL, checking size and SHA-256. Licences use the analysis allowlist (scripts/pipeline/lib/analysis/licences.mjs); items a lawyer still has to review are marked licenceReview: pending (on by default with a warning; video.licenceReview: "strict" turns narration off).

packages.name: kokoro-onnx
packages.why: text to speech (Kokoro-82M on ONNX Runtime, CPU)

packages.name: imageio-ffmpeg
packages.why: a pinned ffmpeg binary for every platform (render, mux)

bundled.name: libsndfile (bundled by soundfile)
bundled.why: loaded unmodified as a shared library; the factory never redistributes it (pip fetches the upstream wheel)

bundled.name: ffmpeg (bundled by imageio-ffmpeg)
bundled.why: the wheel's binary is built with --enable-gpl; run unmodified as a separate program, never linked, never redistributed by the factory. A team may point video.ffmpeg at its own (for example LGPL) build

bundled.name: phonemizer (dependency of kokoro-onnx)
bundled.why: imported by the narration script in its own process; never redistributed by the factory

bundled.name: espeak-ng (bundled by espeakng-loader, dependency of kokoro-onnx)
bundled.why: loaded unmodified as a shared library in the narration process; never redistributed by the factory

voices.why: the voice style vectors; the kokoro-onnx release page does not state their licence separately (Kokoro-82M is Apache-2.0)
